purpose: ASVS V13.1.4 asks documentation to define the secrets critical to the application AND a schedule for rotating them. The first half already existed - cryptographic-key-usage.json enumerates 27 pieces of key material and says for each where it may be used and what it may protect. The second half did not exist at all: no document said when any secret is rotated, and SECRET_ROTATION_REGISTER.md is a scanner report saying nothing is exposed, which is a different question. This pass adds the schedule beside the usage boundary in the same register, renders it for operators, and gates it.
requiredInvariants: The schedule lives beside the usage boundary in one register, never as a second list of secrets. Two lists of secrets drift, and they drift silently.

No single interval is written across every secret. One number would be wrong twice: it overstates what is possible where rotation needs a data migration, and understates what should be done for a token the provider revokes in a second. Each secret records how it can actually be rotated, not only when.

A secret whose rotation requires re-deriving stored data carries no calendar date. GEKTA_PHONE_LOOKUP_PEPPER cannot change without recomputing every blind index, and GEKTA_PHONE_ENCRYPTION_KEY without re-encrypting every stored number. Writing 90 days next to either would be a schedule nobody runs, and a test forbids it explicitly.

Existing rotation capability is recorded as capability, not as a plan: the bank key registry already accepts several keys with validity windows, so BANK_HMAC_SECRET rotates with no downtime, and the auth-mail outbox already runs a versioned keyring.

The register is held to the tree from three sides: a secret with no schedule fails the build, a schedule contradicting its own cadence fails (a calendar with no interval, or an interval with no calendar), and a schedule on configuration - which has nothing to rotate - fails.
The rendered schedule is generated, never hand-edited, and CI regenerates it then refuses a tree where the committed copy differs.

Nothing is claimed beyond the requirement. This is a schedule, not evidence that a rotation happened; the requirement asks for documentation and that is what is delivered. Whether an operator carried out a rotation is not asserted anywhere.

No dependency, schema, migration, RLS or policy change. No secret value is read, written, printed or rotated by this pass. No registration, 1C, marketing or presentation code. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Measured: 27 register entries, 23 of kind secret and 4 configuration. All 23 secrets now carry a rotation record; the 4 configuration entries carry none and are forbidden from carrying one.

19 secrets rotate on a calendar across three different intervals (30, 90, 180 days), 2 are event-driven because their rotation needs a data migration, and 2 are per-run acceptance-only material that does not exist in production.

Five mutations each turn the suite red: dropping one secret's schedule, flattening every secret to one interval, claiming a calendar date for the blind-index pepper, blanking a rationale, and disabling the rotation audit entirely.

V13.1.4 PASS is machine-revocable: five mutations applied with the matrix rebuilt each time - untracking the schedule, erasing the migration-required honesty from the rendered text, downgrading the migration class in the register, disabling the unscheduled-secret check, and removing the CI staleness check - all five drove the verdict to NOT_ASSESSED.
Matrix on this head: PASS 129 -> 130, FAIL 90 -> 89. Exactly one verdict changed; no collateral drift.
scripts/security suite 153/153 green; decision-evidence and web-unit-coverage gates green; sbom-scan.yml parses and runs the new check.
